cohort: Preterm infants ≤35 weeks gestation and ≤2500g birth weight who received parenteral nutrition, survived >1 week, and had no major congenital anomalies, admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit.
finding: Infants exposed to parenteral phosphorus dose restriction had lower serum phosphorus levels, higher serum alkaline phosphatase levels, and required greater inotropic support, particularly those with birth weight >1250g.
birth_weight: ≤2500g, with specific analysis for subgroups <1250g and >1250g.
